summary: The NATO Shield Act requires the President to consult with and report to Congress before taking any action to withdraw the United States from the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO). It mandates that any withdrawal action expires after 30 days unless Congress passes a joint resolution approving it, and prohibits using federal funds to carry out a terminated withdrawal.

affected_groups.effect: Must follow mandatory consultation, reporting, and restriction procedures if considering or initiating withdrawal from NATO.
Gain specific oversight, reporting, approval powers, expedited legislative procedures, and the ability to bring a federal court action for violations.
Prohibited from using federal funds to implement or continue any unauthorized or terminated withdrawal action.

key_provisions: The President must consult with Congress within 72 hours of considering a NATO withdrawal action, determining a cabinet member is considering it, or beginning a plan to withdraw.
The President must submit a report to Congress within 48 hours of initiating a withdrawal action, providing legal justifications, strategic rationales, and expected military and alliance effects.

A withdrawal action automatically ends after 30 days unless Congress passes a joint resolution approving it, or Congress can direct the termination of the withdrawal via joint resolution during that 30-day period.
Federal funds cannot be used to implement or continue any withdrawal action that has been terminated by expiration or by congressional joint resolution.
Establishes expedited congressional committee and floor procedures for considering joint resolutions regarding a withdrawal action.
Allows individual Members of Congress to bring a legal action in a Federal district court for violations of this section, with expedited court review required.
missing_information: The text does not specify exact penalties for executive branch officials beyond the prohibition of federal funds and potential federal court actions brought by Members of Congress.
The text does not mention any prior legislation being repealed or amended.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The NATO Shield Act requires the President to consult with and report to Congress before taking any action to withdraw the United States from the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO). It mandates that any withdrawal action expires after 30 days unless Congress passes a joint resolution approving it, and prohibits using federal funds to carry out a terminated withdrawal.
summary_detail.significance: The bill changes the executive and legislative balance of power regarding international treaties by ensuring that withdrawal from a mutual defense treaty like NATO requires congressional participation and approval. The significance score is 65 because it establishes strict procedural and funding limits on presidential treaty withdrawal authority, impacting national security and foreign policy processes.
